reasons: The rule expects a liability cap and the cited paragraphs (Section 9 Warranties heading, Section 10 General Provisions, 10.8) plus the stated searches support that no cap, damages exclusion or aggregate-liability language exists, so 'missing' is the correct classification.

The inserted 10.9 tracks the playbook's preferred position closely: mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable by the Company and USD 1,000,000, mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, uncapped Excluded Claims for confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmation that Company payment obligations are not 'damages'.

Placement is sensible and minimally invasive — a new subsection appended after 10.8 in General Provisions, with no rewriting of existing text; deterministic checks confirm the cap basis and that no unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, states the position and offers the fallback (straight 12-month fee cap with core carve-outs); the fee basis (30% of Net Sales) is confirmed non-illusory, so the cap is meaningful rather than nominal.
